    Jiahong Xiang, Kunqiu Chen, Lingming Zhang, Yuqun Zhang

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    Spine organizes agent context as a persistent subtask tree, retaining unfinished work and compiling completed subtasks into concise results; evaluations show improved coding performance and lower cost. Its central contribution is agent context and execution architecture, with a partial connection to compositional structure but no direct contribution to internal model mechanisms or reasoning methods.

    Spine 将智能体上下文组织为持久化的子任务树，保留未完成的工作，并将已完成子任务编译为简洁结果；评估显示其编码性能有所提升且成本更低。其核心贡献在于智能体上下文和执行架构，与组合结构有一定关联，但并未直接贡献于模型内部机制或推理方法。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Long-horizon coding tasks contain nested subtasks. Typically, agents record interactions sequentially into a growing history, causing context inflation and performance degradation. Compressing or trimming the history without explicit subtask boundaries can discard information needed by unfinished subtasks. Conversely, recursive subagent delegation isolates completed subtasks through child agents by assigning every subtask boundary to delegation, which conflates subtask granularity with executing agent choice, adding execution and coordination overhead. We introduce Spine, an interface and runtime that align model context with subtask nesting and completion. An agent declares explicit subtask boundaries through work scopes, allowing the same agent to execute nested subtasks inline while reserving delegation for independent parallel tasks. The runtime organizes execution in SpineTree, a persistent tree recording subtask relations, local interactions, completion states, and returned results. Before each model call, it compiles the tree into model context just in time, retaining unfinished subtasks' interactions and replacing completed subtasks' details with their results, while preserving prefix-cache reuse. We integrate Spine into Codex to build SpineCodex. With GPT-5.6 Sol, compared with native Codex, SpineCodex improves SWE-Milestone Score by 11.8% while reducing total cost by 32.4%, improves the average ProgramBench test-pass rate by 17.3%, and improves Mean@5 on eight of the ten evaluated FrontierSWE tasks. On SWE-Milestone, it also achieves a comparable Score to Recursive Subagent at 73.7% lower total cost. We also integrate Spine into Pi through a reusable software package: with Gemini 3.8 Flash and Qwen 3.8 27B, it improves SWE-Milestone Score by 9.5-17.5% and the average ProgramBench test-pass rate by 4.3-8.7% compared with native Pi.

    中文

    长时程编码任务包含嵌套子任务。通常，智能体会将交互按顺序记录到不断增长的历史中，导致上下文膨胀和性能下降。在没有明确子任务边界的情况下压缩或裁剪历史，可能会丢弃未完成子任务所需的信息。相反，通过递归委派子智能体，利用子智能体隔离已完成的子任务，这种做法将每个子任务边界都与委派绑定，从而混淆了子任务粒度与执行智能体的选择，并增加执行和协调开销。我们推出 Spine，这是一种使模型上下文与子任务嵌套及完成状态相匹配的接口和运行时。智能体通过工作作用域声明明确的子任务边界，使同一智能体能够内联执行嵌套子任务，同时仅将独立的并行任务委派出去。运行时通过 SpineTree 组织执行；这是一棵持久化树，记录子任务关系、局部交互、完成状态和返回结果。每次调用模型之前，它都会即时将树编译为模型上下文，保留未完成子任务的交互，并用结果替换已完成子任务的细节，同时保持前缀缓存复用。我们将 Spine 集成到 Codex 中，构建了 SpineCodex。使用 GPT-5.6 Sol 时，与原生 Codex 相比，SpineCodex 将 SWE-Milestone Score 提高了 11.8%，同时将总成本降低了 32.4%，将 ProgramBench 平均测试通过率提高了 17.3%，并在评估的十项 FrontierSWE 任务中有八项提升了 Mean@5。在 SWE-Milestone 上，它还以低 73.7% 的总成本取得了与 Recursive Subagent 相当的 Score。我们还通过一个可复用的软件包将 Spine 集成到 Pi 中：使用 Gemini 3.8 Flash 和 Qwen 3.8 27B 时，与原生 Pi 相比，SWE-Milestone Score 提高了 9.5-17.5%，ProgramBench 平均测试通过率提高了 4.3-8.7%。

    Beyond the Readout: A Latent Numerical Frame Shared Across Modality and Operation

    超越读出：跨模态与操作共享的潜在数值框架

    Oriol Juan Sabater, Alex Ferrando de las Morenas, Pau Rodr\'iguez, Xavier Suau

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    The paper uses causal interventions to identify a shared numerical representation across modalities and operations, including hidden directions that preserve a number for later digit generation. This directly advances mechanistic interpretability; the arithmetic and multi-step output provide some reasoning relevance, while cross-modal alignment alone does not establish compositional generalization and no system design is studied.

    本文通过因果干预识别跨模态、跨运算共享的数值表征，其中包括能够保留数字以供后续生成的隐藏方向。这直接推动了机制可解释性研究；算术和多步输出也与推理有一定关联，但仅凭跨模态对齐无法证明组合泛化，且本文未研究系统设计。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    When a multimodal model computes 17+35 from text or 91-39 from a rendered image, it produces the same answer, 52. Does it use one internal concept of number for both, or separate machinery for each path? Similarity metrics such as RSA or CKA cannot settle this question. They give the same score to identical and to rotated directions, and two representations can look alike only because both prepare the same output digits. We therefore use causal interventions. For four conditions (text or image, addition or subtraction), we learn a small subspace of Gemma4-12B-it's residual stream in which swapping coordinates swaps the model's answer. The subspaces answer three questions. First, do the conditions write numbers along the same directions? They do not. Reusing a subspace from text in an image on the same operation recovers only 53.2% of its causal effect. A single rotation and rescaling maps one subspace onto the other and raises recovery to 91.4%, so the conditions share one geometry expressed in different coordinates. Second, does this shared geometry only reflect the digit the model is about to print? To test this, we split each subspace into 9 directions that the output layer reads to choose the next digit and 13 directions that it cannot see. The 13 hidden directions still carry the number, yet changing them barely alters the digit being written. Third, what are these hidden directions for? A model must emit a multi-digit answer one digit at a time, so it can compute the full result early and keep it in reserve. When two numbers share their first digit, swapping the number in the hidden directions leaves the digit being written intact and redirects the next digit in 77.6% of cases. The model thus forms an abstract numerical concept upstream and unfolds it across time: multimodal representations share meaning through relational geometry across distinct coordinate frames.

    中文

    当多模态模型根据文本计算 17+35，或根据渲染图像计算 91-39 时，它会得到相同的答案 52。两种情况下，它使用的是同一个内部数概念，还是各自采用不同的处理机制？RSA 或 CKA 等相似度指标无法回答这个问题。对于完全相同的方向和经过旋转的方向，它们给出的分数相同；两种表征看起来相似，也可能只是因为它们都在为输出相同的数字做准备。因此，我们采用因果干预。对于四种条件（文本或图像、加法或减法），我们从 Gemma4-12B-it 的残差流中学习一个小子空间，在其中交换坐标会交换模型的答案。这些子空间可以回答三个问题。第一，不同条件是否沿相同方向写入数字？并非如此。在同一运算下，将文本中的子空间用于图像，只能恢复其 53.2% 的因果效应。通过一次旋转和缩放将一个子空间映射到另一个子空间，恢复率可提高到 91.4%；这说明不同条件共享同一种几何结构，只是坐标系不同。第二，这种共享几何结构是否仅反映模型即将输出的数字？为检验这一点，我们将每个子空间分为两部分：输出层读取的 9 个方向用于选择下一个数字，另有 13 个方向对输出层不可见。这 13 个隐藏方向仍然承载着数字，但改变它们几乎不会影响正在写出的数字。第三，这些隐藏方向有什么用途？模型必须一次输出一个数字来生成多位答案，因此可以提前算出完整结果并暂存起来。当两个数字的首位相同时，在隐藏方向中交换数字，不会改变正在写出的数字，却会在 77.6% 的情况下改变下一个数字。由此可见，模型会在较早阶段形成抽象数概念，并随时间逐步展开：多模态表征通过不同坐标框架中的关系几何结构共享含义。

We introduce Task Advancement Memory (TAM), which defines task advancement as verified task progress, and supports ongoing task execution and learns reusable operations. During execution, Task Advancement State represents how verified task progress changes the remaining goals, allowing the agent to build on earlier achievements across applications. After each task, advancement supervision identifies and abstracts the interactions that produced a verified local result. The learned operations preserve the relation between required inputs, expected outcomes, and verification conditions. This retains locally successful operations from both successful and failed tasks. On MobileWorld GUI-only tasks, Advancement State alone raises success from 12.0% to 28.2%. Full TAM achieves a 17.6% relative gain in task success over the strongest evaluated baseline and reduces lifecycle tokens per solved task by 38.7%. On SPA-Bench, TAM achieves state-of-the-art task success in the single-app English Level 3 setting.

    The paper develops a collective-instability theory explaining how cross-task coupling can make self-reinforcement collapse in RLVR, then supports key predictions with simulations and Transformer interventions.     阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Label-free reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) rewards a language model for agreeing with its own majority vote. It improves reasoning at first but eventually collapses: the self-assessed reward goes to one while accuracy falls, often until the model gives the same answer to every problem. The collapse appears only when training uses many problems. We explain this dataset-size dependence as a collective instability. In a solvable many-problem model in which problems share parameters, a population whose problems prefer different answers amplifies any shared perturbation for as long as the population-averaged slope $\langle F'\rangle$ of the single-problem self-reinforcement drift $F$ is positive. This holds while problems are still uncertain about their answers. Per-problem sharpening, slowed by $1/N$ for $N$ training problems, races against the shared mode, which grows at a rate $\propto\lambda^2$ independent of $N$, where $\lambda$ is the strength of the shared coupling. This yields a critical number of problems $N_c\simeq\ln(1/\delta)/(\lambda^2G)$, where $\delta$ seeds the shared mode and $G$ decreases with the initial confidence. Simulations of the model confirm the predictions: a sharp transition, $N_c\propto\lambda^{-2}$ up to a logarithmic correction, a single critical amplification $\lambda^2NG$ across couplings, confidence profiles and training variants, a logarithmic dependence on batch size, and no collapse for confident initial models. A kernel version of the theory identifies a protective coupling (generalization of sharpening) and a marginal-entropy bonus that stabilizes the uniform collective mode. In label-free RL of a small Transformer, removing the shared direction prevents collapse entirely, restoring it causes collapse, and collapse grows with training-set size and base-model entropy.

    Chain-of-thought reasoning has substantially advanced video understanding in multimodal large language models (MLLMs). However, language-based reasoning traces do not provide a reliable mechanism for models to revisit relevant visual evidence, leading to visual forgetting and impairing their ability to reason over video content. Existing approaches maintain visual grounding during reasoning in two main ways: they either refer to evidence using textual coordinates, which specify symbolic locations rather than the visual content itself, or reinsert cropped regions or frames into the multimodal context, preserving visual details at the cost of substantial context expansion. To address these limitations, we introduce VideoLVR, which constructs latent visual evidence from local regions at relevant video moments, thereby providing visual support for intermediate reasoning steps. To supervise latent visual evidence generation, we introduce a visual token prediction objective that formulates visual token reconstruction as prediction over a vocabulary derived from the input video, thereby unifying visual evidence reconstruction and text generation within the same token prediction framework. This shared prediction framework enables MLLMs to reason over interleaved text tokens and latent visual states while integrating evidence from different moments. We further extend VideoLVR to reinforcement learning by treating sampled visual tokens as actions alongside text tokens and jointly optimizing the policy using final-answer rewards. By efficiently revisiting task-relevant visual information during reasoning, VideoLVR improves video understanding without substantially expanding the multimodal context. Experiments on multiple video benchmarks demonstrate its effectiveness, especially on tasks requiring fine-grained visual evidence.

    ENGLISH

    Relations compose through the entity they share - Alice is Bob's mother and Bob is Carol's father, so Alice is Carol's grandmother - and the order matters, since a father's mother is not a mother's father; verifying a composed relation means closing the loop. We show that if each entity's coordinate frame may be rotated independently (per-entity frame freedom), three things follow. In the pure-gauge sector, relations that share no cycle cannot interact at all. The only gauge-invariant score of a triangle is a class function of its holonomy $H = T_{ij} T_{jk} T_{ki}$ - a Wilson loop. And the only equivariant update of an edge is $U = \Psi(H)\, T_{ij}$ with $\Psi$ conjugation-equivariant. Edge attention by Wilson loops is therefore not one design among many but the unique form the symmetry permits. Three communities hold pieces of this form: the commuting-operator embeddings of knowledge graphs are its abelian (commuting) sector; AlphaFold's triangle update and the Edge Transformer have its shape - an edge updated through the third vertex - without its constraints; and lattice QCD builds it equivariantly on lattices. We instantiate the equivariant sub-family on general relational graphs as holonomy attention. With no training and composition alone, it infers unobserved $S_4$ relations on sparse graphs at 0.88 with a fifth of the edges corrupted, at or slightly below specialist synchronization algorithms, where every commutative architecture is capped at 0.083; its holonomy score flags corrupted triangles at AUC 0.99 where commuting scores are capped at 0.76 by a second selection rule, and it separates clusters without labels.

    ENGLISH

    Patterns of microcircuitry in the cerebral cortex suggest that the brain has an array of repeated canonical computational units. However, neural representations are distributed, so the relevant computations may only be related indirectly to single-neuron transformations. It thus remains an open challenge how to define canonical distributed computations. Here we integrate normative and algorithmic theories of neural computation to present a mathematical framework for inferring canonical distributed computations from large-scale neural activity patterns. At the normative level, we hypothesize that the brain learns a structured internal model of its environment and its latent causes. At the algorithmic level, we propose that this inference process is a nonlinear message-passing algorithm on a graph-structured model of the world. Given a time series of neural activity during a perceptual inference task, our analysis framework finds (i) the neural representation of the relevant latent variables, (ii) interactions between these latent variables that define the brain's internal model of the world, and (iii) message functions that specify the inference algorithm. With enough data, key computational properties are identifiable due to constraints from the symmetries inherent in any canonical computation, up to a joint global transformation of all interactions and the message-passing functions. As a demonstration of this framework, we analyze artificial neural recordings generated by a simulated brain that implicitly implements an approximate inference algorithm. Given simulated inputs and neural activity we successfully recover the latent variables, their neural representation and dynamics, and canonical message functions that govern the dynamics. Analysis of these models reveals features of experimental design required to extract canonical computations from neural data.

    The availability of a wide range of large language models (LLMs) embedded in various agentic systems has significantly increased the potential of model selection strategies to improve the cost-performance tradeoff. Existing strategies involve either routing, where a single model is chosen per query, or cascading, which sequentially runs increasingly larger models until a satisfactory answer is found. However, current approaches face three key limitations: they (1) lack formal proofs of optimality, (2) fail to identify the conditions under which these strategies are most effective to improve the cost-performance tradeoff, and (3) are unable to combine both paradigms for further improvements. To address these issues, we first derive a novel optimal strategy for cascading and prove the optimality of an existing routing strategy. Further, we propose cascade routing, a unified framework that integrates routing and cascading into a theoretically optimal strategy. Through our analysis, we identify good quality estimators as the critical factor for the success of model selection paradigms. Finally, in our experiments, we show that cascade routing consistently outperforms the individual approaches by a large margin and we analyze quality estimators to determine when routing and/or cascading are useful paradigms for model selection.

    Prescribed-parameter convolutional transforms achieve strong time series classification performance using fixed kernels, simple pooling operations, and a linear classifier. We establish exact invariance to circular translations under periodic boundaries and quantify departures from invariance under finite boundaries. We then define the population pairwise geometry induced by a distribution of convolutional parameters and show how a finite random kernel bank concentrates around that geometry. This separates the role of the parameter distribution from the number of sampled kernels. Increasing kernel count produces diminishing representational gains. Increasing kernel length generally raises effective dimensionality and distance correlation, while the best test performance occurs at intermediate lengths and training accuracy remains close to perfect. Together, these results support an interpretation in which nonlinear pooling creates a richer but structured representation that can favour linear separation, while further representational richness need not improve generalisation.

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly trained to abstain from answering questions they are unsure about. However, this ability is often misapplied: in real-world applications, user prompts sometimes contain elements of uncertainty, which lead LLMs to abstain even on problems they are capable of solving. We argue that LLM abstention is not only an expression of genuine uncertainty; it can also be an artifact largely shaped by prompts. We name this phenomenon *Abstention Inflation*. We add "Unknown" as an extra option for LLMs to choose from; experiments show serious accuracy drops on True/False Questions (TFQs). Replacing "Unknown" with an unrelated random word produces a similar effect. We argue that LLMs are trained to imitate the surface pattern of abstention, rather than to express genuine uncertainty. Based on ten experimental settings, we support four claims that form a progressive argument: **(C1)** *Abstention Inflation* can be triggered by the presence of an extra option, not by genuine uncertainty; **(C2)** it makes the models deny they can answer, even when they can; **(C3)** it is a later-layer output override, as the reasoning traces and mid-layer representations preserve correct answers; **(C4)** it is not stochastic noise: it results from various factors, emerges through instruction tuning, is boosted by problems' higher difficulty, and can be mitigated at larger model sizes.

    本文从理论上分析了抽样对概念激活向量的影响，发现其方差大致按 1/N 下降，并通过涵盖四种模态的实验加以验证。这为理解基于概念的模型表示解释提供了可迁移的见解，但并未直接研究内部机制或表示几何结构。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    One of the most pressing challenges in artificial intelligence is to make models more transparent to their users. Recently, explainable artificial intelligence has come up with numerous methods to tackle this challenge. A promising avenue is to use concept-based explanations, that is, high-level concepts instead of plain feature importance scores. Among this class of methods, Concept Activation Vectors (CAVs, Kim et al., 2018) stand out as one of the main protagonists. One interesting aspect of CAVs is that their computation requires sampling random examples from the train set. Therefore, the actual vectors obtained may vary depending on the randomness of this sampling. In this paper, we propose a fine-grained theoretical analysis of CAV construction in order to quantify their variability. Our results, confirmed by experiments on several real-life datasets of four different modalities, point to an universal result: the variance of CAVs declines roughly as $1/N$, where $N$ is the number of random examples. Based on this, we give practical recommendations for a resource-efficient application of the method.

    Yang Liu, Yunjiang Jiang, Ayush Agarwal, Yihan Wu, Haoran Liu, Bi Xue

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    The paper introduces link embeddings and linear XOR attention to reduce recommendation inference cost as histories and candidate sets grow.     阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Scaling large recommendation systems requires advancing three major frontiers: processing longer user histories, expanding candidate sets, and increasing model capacity. While promising, transformers' computational cost scales quadratically with the user sequence length and linearly with the number of candidates. This trade-off makes it prohibitively expensive to expand candidate sets or increase sequence length at inference, despite the significant performance improvements. We introduce \textbf{LIME}, a novel architecture that resolves this trade-off. Through two key innovations, LIME fundamentally reduces computational complexity. First, low-rank ``link embeddings" enable pre-computation of attention weights by decoupling user and candidate interactions, making the inference cost nearly independent of candidate set size. Second, a linear attention mechanism, \textbf{LIME-XOR}, reduces the complexity with respect to user sequence length from quadratic ($O(N^2)$) to linear ($O(N)$). Experiments on public and industrial datasets show LIME achieves near-parity with state-of-the-art transformers but with a 10$\times$ inference speedup on large candidate sets or long sequence lengths. When tested on a major recommendation platform, LIME improved user engagement while maintaining minimal inference costs with respect to candidate set size and user history length, establishing a new paradigm for efficient and expressive recommendation systems.

    ENGLISH

    Planning with world models offers a powerful paradigm for robotic control. Conventional approaches train a model to predict future frames conditioned on current frames and actions, which can then be used for planning. However, the objective of predicting future pixels is often at odds with the actual planning objective; strong pixel reconstruction does not always correlate with good planning decisions. This paper posits that instead of reconstructing future frames as pixels, world models only need to predict task-relevant semantic information about the future. For such prediction the paper poses world modeling as a visual question answering problem about semantic information in future frames. This perspective allows world modeling to be approached with the same tools underlying vision language models. Thus, vision-language models can be trained as "semantic" world models through a supervised finetuning process on image-action-text data, enabling planning for decision-making while inheriting many of the generalization and robustness properties from the pretrained vision-language models. In this paper, we introduce this new method and validate it on simulated robotic tasks leading to improvements over typical paradigms of reconstruction-based action-conditional world modeling. Website available at https://weirdlabuw.github.io/swm.

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    ENGLISH

    Language agents are moving from single-user assistants to shared collaborators in workspaces, forums, and group chats. A shared agent observes interleaved messages from multiple users, maintains persistent context, and executes tool actions, creating a boundary problem absent from standard single-user agents: the agent must decide not only whether an instruction is safe, but which user or task it is allowed to govern. We identify cross-user poisoning (CUP), where an adversary injects a message into shared context that is later applied while the agent serves a benign user, causing unauthorized actions or responses outside the instruction's intended scope. We validate CUP on two deployed multi-user agents, Continua and ElizaOS, and introduce MURMUR, a framework for evaluating shared-context agents under concurrent multi-user interactions. Across Slack, Workspace, and Airline domains, CUP achieves high attack success, persists across later interactions, and remains substantially more effective than matched prompt-injection attacks. We evaluate boundary-scoping defenses and find that context summarization alone is insufficient, while task clustering and provenance prompting substantially reduce non-adaptive propagation. These results show that robust multi-user agents require explicit user/task scoping rather than generic input filtering or context compression.

    Large language model (LLM)-driven agents are emerging as a powerful new paradigm for solving complex problems. Despite the empirical success of these practices, a theoretical framework to understand and unify their macroscopic dynamics remains lacking. This paper proposes a method based on the least action principle to estimate the underlying generative directionality of LLMs embedded within agents. By experimentally measuring the transition probabilities between LLM-generated states, we report evidence consistent with a tendency toward detailed balance in LLM-generated transitions, indicating that LLM generation may not be achieved by generally learning rule sets and strategies, but rather by implicitly learning a class of underlying potential functions that may transcend different LLM architectures and prompt templates. To our knowledge, this provides an effective macroscopic description of LLM generative dynamics that does not depend on specific model details. This work is an attempt to establish a macroscopic dynamics theory of complex AI systems, aiming to elevate the study of AI agents from a collection of engineering practices to a science built on effective measurements that are predictable and quantifiable.

    Yu-Chen Lu, Sheng-Feng Yu, Hui-Hsien Weng, Pei-Shuo Wang, Yu-Fang Hu, Liang Hung-Chun, Hung-Yueh Chiang, Kai-Chiang Wu

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    SkipCat introduces shared low-rank projections and block skipping to preserve model performance while reducing memory and computation for deployment. Its contribution advances efficient model computation, while shared projections are a compression technique rather than substantive evidence about compositional representations.

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Large language models (LLM) have achieved remarkable performance across a wide range of tasks. However, their substantial parameter sizes pose significant challenges for deployment on edge devices with limited computational and memory resources. Low-rank compression is a promising approach to address this issue, as it reduces both computational and memory costs, making LLM more suitable for resource-constrained environments. Nonetheless, na\"ive low-rank compression methods require a significant reduction in the retained rank to achieve meaningful memory and computation savings. For a low-rank model, the ranks need to be reduced by more than half to yield efficiency gains. Such aggressive truncation, however, typically results in substantial performance degradation. To address this trade-off, we propose SkipCat, a novel low-rank compression framework that enables the use of higher ranks while achieving the same compression rates. First, we introduce an intra-layer shared low-rank projection method, where multiple matrices that share the same input use a common projection. This reduces redundancy and improves compression efficiency. Second, we propose a block skipping technique that omits computations and memory transfers for selected sub-blocks within the low-rank decomposition. These two techniques jointly enable our compressed model to retain more effective ranks under the same compression budget. Experimental results show that, without any additional fine-tuning, our method outperforms previous low-rank compression approaches by 7% accuracy improvement on zero-shot tasks under the same compression rate. These results highlight the effectiveness of our rank-maximized compression strategy in preserving model performance under tight resource constraints.

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    The paper proposes a reusable semantic-geometric representation that combines task structure with object relations and motion histories, supporting transfer across embodiments and variable task sequences.     阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Learning structured task representations from human demonstrations is essential for bimanual manipulation, where action ordering, object involvement, and interaction geometry vary significantly across executions. A key challenge lies in jointly capturing the discrete semantic task structure and the temporal evolution of object-centric geometric relations in a form that supports reasoning over task progression. We introduce a semantic-geometric graph-based task representation that jointly encodes object identities, inter-object semantic relations, and per-object motion histories, via a Message Passing Neural Network (MPNN) encoder and a Transformer-based decoder. The encoder operates solely on the temporal scene graph, producing structured representations decoupled from action labels. The decoder then conditions on action-context to forecast future actions, associated objects, and object motions. This decoupling learns task-agnostic representations, enabling encoder reuse across embodiments through decoder-only finetuning on a small robot dataset. Across eleven bimanual tasks from two datasets, we find that the benefit of structured semantic--geometric representations over simpler sequence-based models grows with task variability in action ordering and object involvement. At deployment, a planner couples the action and motion predictions with learned Probabilistic Movement Primitives, achieving full task success on two real-robot bimanual tasks and outperforming graph ablations, Transformer, decoder-only, and finetuned vision-language model baselines.

    本文的主要贡献是面向卫星影像定量空间推理的 SQuID 基准和 QASR 基线，实验结果表明分割是一个关键错误来源。它对多步空间推理进行了实质性评估，但组合能力是次要方面，而智能体编写程序的方法本身提供的系统洞见有限。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Vision-Language Models (VLMs) describe satellite images fluently but struggle with the quantitative spatial reasoning that remote sensing (RS) analysts perform routinely, such as counting buildings, measuring forest area in hectares and computing distances in meters. We introduce SQuID (Satellite Quantitative Intelligence Dataset), a benchmark of 2,000 questions over 587 images from four sources at 0.3 to 1.0 m ground sampling distance, covering 24 question types in three difficulty tiers. Answers are computed from curated segmentation masks or, for 50 questions, from human consensus, and numeric answers are scored against tolerance ranges informed by human annotations. SQuID also releases the reference masks behind its answers, so that modular systems can be evaluated using reference rather than predicted masks, and 75,687 training question-answer pairs on disjoint images (SQuID-Train). Among 15 evaluated systems, the best zero-shot end-to-end VLM reaches 28.1%, and RS-specialized VLMs score lower. As a baseline, we propose QASR (Quantitative Agentic Spatial Reasoning), in which an LLM writes a program that segments the image and measures the masks with geometric operators. QASR reaches 42.0%. On the 1,950 mask-derived questions, running its programs on the reference masks instead of predicted masks raises accuracy from 42.2% to 82.6%, so segmentation is its main source of error. Fine-tuning Qwen2.5-VL-7B on SQuID-Train raises its accuracy from 16.1% to 40.7%, close to QASR. Multi-condition questions (Tier 3) remain the hardest in every setting, at 62.0% for QASR with reference masks and 13.2% after fine-tuning. These results leave clear room for end-to-end models that learn metric spatial reasoning, and SQuID provides the data to train and evaluate them.

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Recent work has revealed a link between self-attention mechanisms in transformers and test-time kernel regression via the Nadaraya-Watson estimator, with standard softmax attention corresponding to a Gaussian kernel. However, a kernel-theoretic understanding of sparse attention mechanisms is currently missing. In this paper, we establish a formal correspondence between sparse attention and compact (bounded support) kernels. We show that normalized ReLU and sparsemax attention arise from Epanechnikov kernel regression under fixed and adaptive normalizations, respectively. More generally, we demonstrate that widely used kernels in nonparametric density estimation -- including Epanechnikov, biweight, and triweight -- correspond to $\alpha$-entmax attention with $\alpha = 1 + \frac{1}{n}$ for $n \in \mathbb{N}$, while the softmax/Gaussian relationship emerges in the limit $n \to \infty$. This unified perspective explains how sparsity naturally emerges from kernel design and provides principled alternatives to heuristic top-$k$ attention and other associative memory mechanisms. Experiments with a kernel-regression-based variant of transformers -- Memory Mosaics -- show that kernel-based sparse attention achieves competitive performance on language modeling, in-context learning, and length generalization tasks, offering a principled framework for designing attention mechanisms.

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Learning a common policy from multiple source environments requires accounting for cross-source heterogeneity, and the offline setting introduces an additional challenge of limited data coverage. We formulate this problem as a distributionally robust Markov decision process under a shared linear MDP representation with source-specific transition and reward components. The uncertainty set is constructed through feature-wise mixtures of these components, yielding a $d$-rectangular structure that captures cross-source heterogeneity and admits a robust Bellman recursion. Building on this formulation, we develop Group-Robust Pessimistic Value Iteration (GR-PEVI), an offline policy-learning algorithm that combines feature-wise worst-case aggregation with a data-dependent pessimism penalty. Under a robust partial coverage condition, we establish finite-sample suboptimality guarantees for GR-PEVI and extend the analysis to clustered sources, characterizing the trade-off between the statistical gain from pooling similar sources and the approximation error induced by within-cluster heterogeneity. Simulation studies demonstrate the effectiveness of GR-PEVI, with empirical behavior consistent with the theoretical analysis. We apply GR-PEVI to a multi-source electronic health record study of multiple sclerosis treatment decisions to illustrate its use in a clinical setting.

    The advancement of Large Language Models (LLMs) has catalyzed the development of autonomous agents capable of navigating complex environments. However, existing evaluations primarily adopt a deductive paradigm, where agents execute tasks based on explicitly provided rules and static goals, often within limited planning horizons. Crucially, this neglects the inductive necessity for agents to discover latent transition laws from experience autonomously, which is the cornerstone for enabling agentic foresight and sustaining strategic coherence. To bridge this gap, we introduce OdysseyArena, which re-centers agent evaluation on long-horizon, active, and inductive interactions. We formalize and instantiate four primitives, translating abstract transition dynamics into concrete interactive environments. Building upon this, we establish OdysseyArena-Lite for standardized benchmarking, providing a set of 120 tasks to measure an agent's inductive efficiency and long-horizon discovery. Pushing further, we introduce OdysseyArena-Challenge to stress-test agent stability across extreme interaction horizons (e.g., > 200 steps). Project homepage: https://os-copilot.github.io/OdysseyArena-Home/

    中文

    大型语言模型（LLM）的进步推动了能够在复杂环境中导航的自主智能体的发展。然而，现有评估主要采用演绎范式：智能体依据明确提供的规则和静态目标执行任务，规划时域通常也有限。关键问题在于，这忽略了智能体通过经验自主发现潜在转移规律的归纳需求，而这正是实现智能体前瞻能力并维持策略连贯性的基石。为弥补这一空缺，我们推出 OdysseyArena，将智能体评估的重点重新放在长时程、主动和归纳式交互上。我们将四种基本要素形式化并实例化，把抽象的转移动力学转化为具体的交互环境。在此基础上，我们建立了用于标准化基准测试的 OdysseyArena-Lite，提供 120 项任务，用于衡量智能体的归纳效率和长时程发现能力。进一步地，我们推出 OdysseyArena-Challenge，用于在极长交互时域（例如超过 200 步）下对智能体稳定性进行压力测试。对 15 个以上领先 LLM 的大量实验表明，即使是前沿模型在归纳场景中也存在不足，揭示了实现复杂环境中自主发现的一个关键瓶颈。项目主页：https://os-copilot.github.io/OdysseyArena-Home/

    Difficulty-Estimated Policy Optimization

    基于难度估计的策略优化

    Yu Zhao, Fan Jiang, Tianle Liu, Bo Zeng, Xintong Wang, Jiaxuan Teng, Yu Liu, Yichao Du

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    DEPO trains reasoning models by estimating sample difficulty and filtering low-utility rollouts, improving training efficiency and benchmark performance. This is a strong contribution to reasoning training; its compute allocation is a meaningful but secondary systems contribution, with no interpretability or compositional insight described.

    DEPO 通过估计样本难度并筛除低效用 rollout 来训练推理模型，从而提高训练效率和基准性能。这是对推理训练的有力贡献；其计算资源分配也有意义，但属于次要的系统贡献，且文中没有描述可解释性或组合性方面的洞见。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Recent advancements in Large Reasoning Models (LRMs), exemplified by DeepSeek-R1, have underscored the potential of scaling inference-time compute through Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO). However, GRPO frequently suffers from gradient signal attenuation when encountering problems that are either too trivial or overly complex. In these scenarios, the disappearance of inter-group advantages makes the gradient signal susceptible to noise, thereby jeopardizing convergence stability. While variants like DAPO attempt to rectify gradient vanishing, they do not alleviate the substantial computational overhead incurred by exhaustive rollouts on low-utility samples. In this paper, we propose Difficulty-Estimated Policy Optimization (DEPO), a novel framework designed to optimize the efficiency and robustness of reasoning alignment. DEPO integrates an online Difficulty Estimator that dynamically assesses and filters training data before the rollout phase. This mechanism ensures that computational resources are prioritized for samples with high learning potential. Empirical results show that DEPO achieves approximately 1.86x faster rollouts than DAPO in the profiled configuration, while improving benchmark performance over GRPO at comparable training cost. Our approach significantly lowers the computational barrier for training high-performance reasoning models, offering a more sustainable path for reasoning scaling.

    中文

    以 DeepSeek-R1 为代表的大型推理模型（LRM）近期进展，凸显了通过组相对策略优化（GRPO）扩展推理时计算的潜力。然而，GRPO 在遇到过于简单或过于复杂的问题时，经常出现梯度信号衰减。在这些情形下，组间优势消失，使梯度信号容易受到噪声影响，从而危及收敛稳定性。DAPO 等变体试图解决梯度消失问题，但无法降低对低效用样本进行穷举式 rollout 所带来的大量计算开销。本文提出难度估计策略优化（DEPO），这是一种旨在提升推理对齐效率与稳健性的新框架。DEPO 集成了一个在线难度估计器，在 rollout 阶段之前动态评估并筛选训练数据。该机制确保计算资源优先用于学习潜力高的样本。实验结果表明，在所分析的配置下，DEPO 的 rollout 速度约为 DAPO 的 1.86 倍，同时在训练成本相当的情况下，基准性能优于 GRPO。我们的方法显著降低了训练高性能推理模型的计算门槛，为推理扩展提供了更可持续的路径。

    Reinforced Fast Weights via Next-Sequence Prediction

    通过下一序列预测强化快速权重

    Hee Seung Hwang, Xindi Wu, Sanghyuk Chun, Olga Russakovsky, Zhiwei Deng

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    ReFINE trains fast-weight models to use recurrent memory for coherent multi-token continuations, using entropy-selected rollouts and sequence-level rewards. This is a substantial algorithmic contribution to long-context reasoning and memory-based computation, but the abstract does not study internal representations or compositional generalization.

    ReFINE 通过基于熵选择的 rollout 和序列级奖励来训练快速权重模型利用循环记忆生成连贯的多词元续写。这是对长上下文推理和基于记忆的计算的一项重要算法贡献，但摘要没有研究内部表征或组合泛化。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Fast weight architectures offer a promising alternative to standard transformers for long-context modeling by replacing the KV-cache with a recurrently updated fixed-size memory. Despite this architectural shift, they are typically trained with the same next-token prediction (NTP) objective as standard transformers. This creates a mismatch: fast weight models rely on an evolving memory state to support future predictions, while NTP provides only token-level supervision for the immediate next token. We address this mismatch with next-sequence prediction (NSP), a sequence-level extension of NTP that trains models to produce coherent multi-token continuations from their recurrent memory state. To optimize this sequence-level objective, we propose ReFINE (Reinforced Fast weIghts via Next sEquence prediction). ReFINE selects informative token positions based on prediction entropy, generates multi-token rollouts, assigns sequence-level rewards, and optimizes the model with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO). ReFINE is applicable throughout the training lifecycle of pre-trained language models: mid-training, post-training, and test-time training. Experiments on LaCT-760M and DeltaNet-1.3B show that ReFINE consistently outperforms NTP-based supervised fine-tuning in needle-in-a-haystack retrieval, long-context question answering, and diverse tasks in LongBench. ReFINE provides an effective and versatile framework for improving long-context modeling in fast weight architectures.

    中文

    快速权重架构为长上下文建模提供了标准 Transformer 的一种有前景的替代方案，其做法是用循环更新的定长记忆取代 KV 缓存。尽管架构发生了这种变化，它们通常仍使用与标准 Transformer 相同的下一词元预测（NTP）目标进行训练。这造成了不匹配：快速权重模型依赖不断演变的记忆状态来支持未来预测，而 NTP 仅针对紧接着的下一个词元提供词元级监督。我们通过下一序列预测（NSP）来解决这一不匹配；NSP 是 NTP 的序列级扩展，训练模型从其循环记忆状态生成连贯的多词元续写。为优化这一序列级目标，我们提出 ReFINE（通过下一序列预测强化快速权重）。ReFINE 根据预测熵选择信息量高的词元位置，生成多词元 rollout，分配序列级奖励，并通过组相对策略优化（GRPO）优化模型。ReFINE 适用于预训练语言模型训练生命周期的各个阶段：中期训练、后训练和测试时训练。在 LaCT-760M 和 DeltaNet-1.3B 上的实验表明，在大海捞针式检索、长上下文问答以及 LongBench 的多种任务中，ReFINE 始终优于基于 NTP 的监督微调。ReFINE 为改进快速权重架构的长上下文建模提供了有效且灵活的框架。

    AgentSentry: Mitigating Indirect Prompt Injection in LLM Agents via Temporal Causal Diagnostics and Context Purification

    AgentSentry：通过时序因果诊断与上下文净化缓解 LLM 智能体中的间接提示注入

    Tian Zhang, Yiwei Xu, Juan Wang, Keyan Guo, Xiaoyang Xu, Bowen Xiao, Quanlong Guan, Jinlin Fan, Jiawei Liu, Zhiquan Liu and Hongxin Hu

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    AgentSentry introduces boundary-local counterfactual diagnostics and context purification to attribute and mitigate prompt injection in multi-step agents. This is a substantial contribution to agent execution and safety, but it does not study internal representations or compositional reasoning mechanisms.

    AgentSentry 引入边界局部反事实诊断和上下文净化，以在多步智能体中归因并缓解提示注入。这是对智能体执行与安全的一项重要贡献，但它没有研究内部表征或组合推理机制。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Tool-augmented large language model (LLM) agents aggregate dialogue history, tool outputs, and retrieved content into an accumulated runtime state to complete multi-step tasks. This execution model exposes agents to indirect prompt injection (IPI) attacks, in which attacker-controlled instructions embedded in external artifacts enter the agent state and later influence tool use. Multi-turn IPI is especially challenging because injected content can persist across steps and trigger unauthorized state-changing actions only after merging with user intent. This creates a source-attribution problem: existing inference-time defenses can often detect suspicious behavior but do not directly distinguish whether a pending action is supported by the user task or influenced by injected content. They therefore resort to conservative blocking, termination, or broad filtering. We propose AgentSentry, an inference-time defense that operationalizes temporal causal diagnostics through boundary-local counterfactual re-executions at tool-return boundaries. It substitutes the mediator under a restored snapshot, records whether the pending proposal survives, and aggregates user-view and probe scores across adjacent boundaries. When a proposal is mediator-sensitive, AgentSentry purifies the implicated mediator content while preserving task-relevant evidence and resumes execution from the sanitized state. We evaluate AgentSentry on AgentDojo across four task suites, three IPI attack families, and three black-box LLM backbones. It records no observed successful attack in the evaluated cases (ASR = 0%) and achieves an average Utility Under Attack (UA) of 76.10%. Over the strongest evaluated baseline, it improves average UA by 1.84--7.60 percentage points, with benign FPRs of 2.06%--5.15%. We further evaluate long-horizon and adaptive attacks, imperfect purification, runtime overhead, and an OpenClaw case study.

    中文

    工具增强型大型语言模型（LLM）智能体会汇总对话历史、工具输出和检索内容，形成累积的运行时状态，以完成多步任务。这种执行模式使智能体暴露于间接提示注入（IPI）攻击之下：嵌入外部材料中的攻击者控制指令进入智能体状态，随后影响工具使用。多轮 IPI 尤具挑战性，因为注入内容可能跨步骤持续存在，并且只有在与用户意图合并后才触发未经授权的状态变更操作。这造成了来源归因问题：现有推理时防御通常能够检测可疑行为，却不能直接区分待执行操作是由用户任务支持，还是受注入内容影响。因此，它们往往采取保守拦截、终止或广泛过滤。我们提出 AgentSentry，这是一种推理时防御方法，通过在工具返回边界进行局部反事实重执行，将时序因果诊断付诸实践。它在恢复的快照下替换中介内容，记录待执行提议是否仍然成立，并汇总相邻边界上的用户视角分数和探测分数。当提议对中介内容敏感时，AgentSentry 会净化相关中介内容，同时保留与任务相关的证据，并从净化后的状态恢复执行。我们在 AgentDojo 上评估 AgentSentry，覆盖四组任务、三类 IPI 攻击和三个黑盒 LLM 主干模型。在所评估案例中未观察到成功攻击（ASR = 0%），且平均攻击下效用（UA）达到 76.10%。与所评估的最强基线相比，其平均 UA 提高了 1.84--7.60 个百分点，良性 FPR 为 2.06%--5.15%。我们还评估了长时程攻击、自适应攻击、不完美净化、运行时开销，并开展了 OpenClaw 案例研究。

    Efficient Token-Level Policy Optimization for Masked Diffusion Models via Velocity Alignment

    通过速度对齐实现掩码扩散模型的高效令牌级策略优化

    Chenxing Wei, Jiazhen Kang, Hong Wang, Jianqing Zhang, Hao Jiang, Xiaolong Xu, Ningyuan Sun, Ying He, F. Richard Yu, Yao Shu, Bo Jiang

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    LFPO proposes token-level policy optimization for masked diffusion language models and shows improved or comparable results on reasoning and coding benchmarks with fewer denoising iterations. Its algorithm directly advances training and inference for reasoning tasks, while benchmark use alone does not establish a contribution to compositional generalization or agent systems.

    LFPO 为掩码扩散语言模型提出了令牌级策略优化，并在推理和编码基准上以更少的去噪迭代取得了更好或相当的结果。其算法直接推动了推理任务的训练和推理发展，而仅使用基准测试并不能证明其对组合泛化或智能体系统有所贡献。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) successfully aligns autoregressive models in rigorous domains like mathematical reasoning and code generation. However, applying RLVR to Diffusion Large Language Models (dLLMs) is hindered by intractable sequence-level likelihoods, forcing existing methods to rely on unstable, high-variance approximations. We propose Sequence Likelihood-Free Policy Optimization (LFPO), an efficient framework that circumvents this bottleneck by formulating policy alignment as discrete velocity alignment. Inspired by continuous flow matching, LFPO eschews trajectory-level estimation and directly optimizes denoising logits via contrastive token-level updates, providing a stable, low-variance surrogate. Furthermore, predicting terminal solutions from intermediate states implicitly straightens the generation trajectory, enabling high-quality sampling with significantly fewer denoising iterations. Extensive experiments on reasoning and coding benchmarks demonstrate that LFPO matches or exceeds the accuracy of likelihood-based baselines while substantially accelerating inference.

    中文

    带可验证奖励的强化学习（RLVR）成功地在数学推理和代码生成等要求严格的领域中对自回归模型进行对齐。然而，将 RLVR 应用于扩散大语言模型（dLLMs）受到难以处理的序列级似然的阻碍，迫使现有方法依赖不稳定且高方差的近似。我们提出序列无似然策略优化（LFPO），这是一种高效框架，通过将策略对齐表述为离散速度对齐来绕过这一瓶颈。受连续流匹配的启发，LFPO 摒弃轨迹级估计，直接通过对比式令牌级更新优化去噪 logits，从而提供稳定、低方差的替代目标。此外，从中间状态预测最终解会隐式地拉直生成轨迹，使得以显著更少的去噪迭代实现高质量采样。在推理和编码基准上的大量实验表明，LFPO 的准确率达到或超过基于似然的基线，同时大幅加快推理速度。

    HiAP: A Multi-Granular Stochastic Auto-Pruning Framework for Vision Transformers

    HiAP：面向视觉 Transformer 的多粒度随机自动剪枝框架

    Andy Li, Aiden Durrant, Milan Markovic and Georgios Leontidis

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    HiAP jointly learns pruning gates across multiple ViT structures under a compute budget, making adaptive compute reduction a substantial algorithmic contribution to model systems. The application to vision and use of structural gates alone do not provide evidence about internal representations or compositional generalization.

    HiAP 在计算预算约束下联合学习 ViT 多种结构上的剪枝门控，使自适应降低计算量成为对模型系统的一项重要算法贡献。其视觉应用场景和结构门控本身并不能证明其涉及内部表征或组合泛化。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Vision Transformers require significant computational resources and memory bandwidth, severely limiting their deployment on resource-constrained hardware. Most structured pruning methods reduce theoretical cost effectively, yet they typically operate at a single structural granularity and depend on multi-stage pipelines with importance ranking, auxiliary solvers or post-hoc magnitude thresholding, followed by a separate fine-tuning phase to recover accuracy. We propose Hierarchical Auto-Pruning (HiAP), which casts ViT pruning as a single budget-aware learning problem and jointly allocates sparsity across four granularities in one end-to-end phase. HiAP introduces stochastic Gumbel-Sigmoid gates at macro level (attention heads and FFN blocks) and micro level (intra-head dimensions and FFN neurons), and trains them against the task loss together with an analytical MAC cost term. Two penalty weights set how much compute is removed, while the gates gradually harden into a dense, smaller sub-network at convergence. It does not require importance heuristics, ranking metrics, auxiliary solvers or secondary fine-tuning. On ImageNet, HiAP compresses DeiT-Base to 7.4G MACs at 80.88% top-1 80.40% at 7.8G without distillation and DeiT-Small to 3.1G at 79.33%, competitive with substantially more complex pipelines at matched compute. The structurally pruned network can be accelerated natively on stock kernels, and more than 90% of the theoretical MAC reduction is realized as measured throughput at batch 256 on an A100.

    中文

    视觉 Transformer 需要大量计算资源和内存带宽，严重限制了其在资源受限硬件上的部署。大多数结构化剪枝方法能够有效降低理论计算成本，但通常只在单一结构粒度上操作，并依赖多阶段流程：先进行重要性排序、使用辅助求解器或事后幅值阈值处理，再通过单独的微调阶段恢复准确率。我们提出层次化自动剪枝（HiAP），将 ViT 剪枝视为一个单一的、具备预算感知能力的学习问题，并在一个端到端阶段内联合分配四种粒度的稀疏性。HiAP 在宏观层级（注意力头和 FFN 块）和微观层级（头内维度和 FFN 神经元）引入随机 Gumbel-Sigmoid 门控，并结合解析 MAC 成本项，以任务损失训练这些门控。两个惩罚权重设定要移除多少计算量，而门控会在收敛时逐渐硬化，形成一个稠密但更小的子网络。该方法无需重要性启发式、排序指标、辅助求解器或额外微调。在 ImageNet 上，HiAP 将 DeiT-Base 压缩至 7.4G MACs，top-1 准确率为 80.88%；在无蒸馏情况下，以 7.8G MACs 达到 80.40%；并将 DeiT-Small 压缩至 3.1G MACs，准确率为 79.33%，在计算量匹配时可与复杂得多的流程相媲美。结构化剪枝后的网络可利用现成内核原生加速；在 A100 上批量大小为 256 时，实测吞吐量实现了超过 90% 的理论 MAC 降幅。

    Characterizing WebGPU Dispatch Overhead for LLM Inference Across Four GPU Vendors, Three Backends, and Three Browsers

    跨四家 GPU 厂商、三种后端和三款浏览器刻画 LLM 推理的 WebGPU 调度开销

    J\k{e}drzej Maczan

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    The paper characterizes WebGPU dispatch costs for LLM inference and introduces a benchmarking methodology and backend; its transferable contribution is about inference execution and optimization, supporting a strong Systems score. Neural-network inference is the application context, with no contribution to internal representations, composition, or reasoning.

    本文刻画了 LLM 推理的 WebGPU 调度成本，并引入了一种基准测试方法和后端；其可迁移的贡献在于推理执行与优化，因而支持较高的系统评分。神经网络推理只是应用背景，本文没有涉及内部表征、组合性或推理方面的贡献。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    WebGPU's security-focused design imposes per-operation validation that compounds across the many small dispatches in neural network inference, yet the true cost of this overhead is poorly characterized. We present a systematic characterization of WebGPU dispatch overhead for LLM inference at batch size 1, spanning four GPU vendors (NVIDIA, AMD, Apple, Intel), two native implementations (Dawn, wgpu-native) and three browsers (Chrome, Safari, Firefox), and two model sizes (Qwen2.5-0.5B and 1.5B). Our primary contribution is a sequential-dispatch methodology that reveals naive single-operation benchmarks overestimate dispatch cost by ${\sim}20\times$. The true per-dispatch cost of WebGPU API overhead alone is 24-36 $\mu$s on Vulkan and 32-71 $\mu$s on Metal, while the total per-operation overhead including Python cost is ${\sim}95$~$\mu$s, which turns out to be a distinction critical for optimization. On Vulkan, kernel fusion improves throughput by 53%, while CUDA fusion provides no benefit, confirming that per-operation overhead is a primary differentiator. LLM inference was tested across three major operating systems (Linux, Windows, macOS). We built $\texttt{torch-webgpu}$, a PrivateUse1-based out-of-tree PyTorch backend and an FX-to-WebGPU compiler, which on our reference platform achieves 11--12% of CUDA performance. At dtype-matched float32, RTX PRO 2000 achieves 1.4$\times$ WebGPU's throughput despite ${\sim}6\times$ less compute than RTX 5090. For dispatch overhead, backend choice is the dominant factor, although implementation choice also matters substantially within a backend (2.2$\times$ for Metal). In terms of dispatch vs kernel compute efficiency, we conclude that at batch=1 with the current dispatch-heavy pipeline, per-operation overhead dominates regardless of kernel quality. All code, benchmarks, and raw data are open source.

    中文

    WebGPU 注重安全性的设计要求对每次操作进行验证，这些验证会在神经网络推理中的大量小型调度中累积，但这种开销的真实成本尚未得到充分刻画。我们系统地刻画了批量大小为 1 时 LLM 推理的 WebGPU 调度开销，涵盖四家 GPU 厂商（NVIDIA、AMD、Apple、Intel）、两种原生实现（Dawn、wgpu-native）、三款浏览器（Chrome、Safari、Firefox）以及两种模型规模（Qwen2.5-0.5B 和 1.5B）。我们的主要贡献是一种顺序调度方法，它揭示了朴素的单操作基准测试会将调度成本高估 ${\sim}20\times$。仅计算 WebGPU API 开销时，每次调度的真实成本在 Vulkan 上为 24–36 $\mu$s，在 Metal 上为 32–71 $\mu$s；而包含 Python 成本的每操作总开销为 ${\sim}95$~$\mu$s。事实证明，这一区分对优化至关重要。在 Vulkan 上，内核融合使吞吐量提高 53%，而 CUDA 融合没有带来收益，这证实每操作开销是一个主要差异因素。我们在三种主流操作系统（Linux、Windows、macOS）上测试了 LLM 推理。我们构建了 $\texttt{torch-webgpu}$，这是一个基于 PrivateUse1 的外置 PyTorch 后端和 FX-to-WebGPU 编译器；在我们的参考平台上，它达到了 CUDA 性能的 11–12%。在 dtype 匹配的 float32 下，RTX PRO 2000 的吞吐量是 WebGPU 的 1.4$\times$，尽管其计算能力比 RTX 5090 少 ${\sim}6\times$。对于调度开销，后端选择是主要影响因素，不过同一后端内实现方式的影响也相当显著（Metal 上为 2.2$\times$）。关于调度开销与内核计算效率，我们的结论是，在当前调度密集型流水线中，批量大小为 1 时，无论内核质量如何，每操作开销都占主导地位。所有代码、基准测试和原始数据均已开源。

    Large language models (LLMs) have become increasingly used for various tasks, often coupled with Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting to boost accuracy. Recent work has shown that high label-prediction accuracy does not guarantee correct intermediate reasoning, and the causes of *reasoning flaws* vary from sample to sample, yet existing remedies either focus on a single domain or assume that one flaw type applies uniformly across samples. A simple mitigation method is to provide the model with the correct answer, but we show that this yields no consistent improvement in reasoning quality. This indicates that the problem cannot be fixed by LLMs' awareness of answers, and must instead be addressed through the *structure* of reasoning. Motivated by this, we propose CRAFT (Consensus Reasoning knowledge graph Aggregation for Flaw-aware Trace synthesis), which aggregates the consensus components shared across multiple candidate reasoning traces to synthesize improved ones. CRAFT consistently improves label-prediction accuracy on both logical and mathematical reasoning benchmarks, outperforming most baselines, while its post-processed traces achieve higher quality under fine-grained benchmark evaluation.

    LAnR jointly performs retrieval and generation in latent space and uses a control head to decide when retrieved evidence is sufficient, with experiments showing better efficiency and QA performance.     阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has become a standard approach for enhancing large language models (LLMs) with external knowledge, mitigating hallucinations, and improving factuality. However, existing systems rely on generating natural language queries at each hop and maintaining a strict architectural separation between retriever and generator, preventing them from leveraging the full representational capacity of the LLM. We propose \textbf{LAnR} (Latent Abstraction for RAG), a unified framework in which a single LLM jointly performs encoding, retrieval, and generation entirely within its own latent space. Rather than generating textual queries, LAnR produces dense retrieval vectors from the hidden states of a designated \texttt{[PRED]} token and uses them to match against encoded document representations from the same model. Furthermore, LAnR adaptively decides when sufficient evidence has been retrieved using a lightweight MLP control head over those same hidden states, eliminating both the separate retriever and explicit token-level stopping reasoning. This design is motivated by our empirical observation that answer token entropy reliably signals retrieval sufficiency. Extensive experiments on six QA benchmarks spanning single-hop and multi-hop settings demonstrate that LAnR outperforms existing RAG methods, while achieving improved inference efficiency through reduced number of retrieval calls and tighter model integration.

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    The paper contributes an MoE serving system that replaces activation routing with asynchronous expert-weight gathering and co-designs routing to improve prefill throughput. This is a substantial systems contribution, but it does not investigate model internals, composition, or reasoning.

    本文提出一种 MoE 服务系统，以异步专家权重聚集取代激活路由，并协同设计路由机制来提高预填充吞吐量。这是一项重要的系统贡献，但没有研究模型内部机制、组合性或推理能力。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Production LLM workloads increasingly serve discriminative tasks, such as classification, recommendation, and verification, whose answers are read from the logits of a single prefill pass with no autoregressive decoding. Serving these prefill-only workloads on mixture-of-experts (MoE) models is bottlenecked not by compute but by the distributed execution required to fit the model: existing parallel strategies (tensor, expert, and pipeline parallelism) trade memory pressure for redundant computation, communication, and synchronization, severely degrading MoE prefill serving efficiency. We observe that these overheads stem from coupling expert placement with synchronous activation routing -- a design inherited from the decoding era. The long, compute-bound forward passes of large-batch prefill open a per-layer window wide enough to stream expert weights in the background, replacing per-layer activation AllToAll with asynchronous weight AllGather fully overlapped with computation. We propose ZeRO-Prefill, a prefill-only serving system built on this idea. Its backend, AsyncEP (Asynchronous Expert Parallelism), gathers experts by weight rather than by activation; its co-designed frontend enforces a physically derived saturation threshold through prefix-aware routing and true-FLOPs load tracking. On Qwen3-235B-A22B across four hardware/precision configurations, ZeRO-Prefill delivers 1.34-1.37x throughput over the strongest distributed baseline on real-world workloads and up to 1.59x on long-context synthetic workloads, sustaining 29.8-36.2% per-GPU model FLOPs utilization.

    Jiwan Chung, Heechan Choi, Seon Joo Kim

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    The paper analyzes hidden-state error dynamics in recurrent models, proving limits on robust symbolic state tracking and validating a readability threshold on group tasks. This advances compositional state tracking, reasoning behavior, and recurrent computation, but does not directly investigate learned internal mechanisms enough for a higher MechInterp score.

    本文分析了循环模型中的隐藏状态误差动力学，证明了稳健符号状态跟踪的局限性，并在群任务上验证了可读性阈值。这推动了组合式状态跟踪、推理行为和循环计算的发展，但没有直接深入研究已学习的内部机制，因此机制可解释性评分不应更高。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    The theory of state tracking in recurrent architectures has predominantly focused on expressive capacity: whether a fixed architecture can theoretically realize a set of symbolic transition rules. We argue that equally important is error control, the dynamics governing hidden-state drift along the directions that distinguish symbolic states. We prove that affine recurrent networks, a class of models encompassing State-Space Models and Linear Attention, cannot correct errors along state-separating subspaces once they preserve state representations. Consequently, practical affine trackers do not learn robust state tracking; rather, they learn finite-horizon solutions governed by accumulated state-relevant error. We characterize the mechanics of this failure, showing that tracking remains readable only while the accumulating within-class spread remains small relative to the between-class separation. We demonstrate empirically on group state-tracking tasks that this breakdown is predictable: tracking collapses when the distinguishability ratio crosses the readability threshold. Across trained models, the point of this crossing predicts the horizon at which downstream accuracy fails. These results establish that robust state tracking is determined not only by an architecture's theoretical expressivity but crucially by its error control.

    中文

    循环架构中的状态跟踪理论主要关注表达能力：固定架构在理论上是否能够实现一组符号转移规则。我们认为，同样重要的是误差控制，即隐藏状态沿区分不同符号状态的方向发生漂移的动力学。我们证明，一旦仿射循环网络保留了状态表征，就无法纠正状态分离子空间中的误差；这类模型包括状态空间模型和线性注意力。因此，实际的仿射状态跟踪器并未学会稳健的状态跟踪，而是学会由累积的状态相关误差所支配的有限时域解。我们刻画了这种失效的机制，表明只有当类内扩散的累积幅度相对于类间分离仍然较小时，跟踪结果才保持可读。我们在群状态跟踪任务上的实证结果表明，这种失效具有可预测性：当可区分性比率越过可读性阈值时，跟踪便会崩溃。在训练后的模型中，这一越界点可以预测下游准确率失效的时域。这些结果表明，稳健的状态跟踪不仅取决于架构的理论表达能力，更关键地取决于其误差控制能力。

    The Global Empirical NTK: Self-Referential Bias and Dimensionality of Gradient Descent Learning

    全局经验 NTK：梯度下降学习中的自指偏置与维度

    James Hazelden, Laura Driscoll, Eli Shlizerman, Eric Shea-Brown

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    The paper derives and analyzes the finite-width Global Empirical NTK, showing how internal state dependencies create measurable, state-dependent constraints on gradient-descent learning; this is a substantial contribution to model geometry and learning mechanisms. Its relevance to reasoning is incidental because it studies learning dynamics rather than reasoning capabilities.

    本文推导并分析了有限宽度的全局经验 NTK，展示内部状态依赖关系如何对梯度下降学习形成可测量且依赖状态的约束；这是对模型几何和学习机制的一项重要贡献。其与推理的关联只是附带的，因为本文研究的是学习动力学，而非推理能力。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    In training a neural network with gradient descent (GD), each iteration induces a linear operator that governs the first-order updates to a model's internal state variables. We call this operator the Global Empirical Neural Tangent Kernel (GeNTK). In finite-width networks, GeNTK is typically intractable to form, leading prior work to focus on restrictive settings, such as tracking only outputs or infinite-width limits. Here, we bridge this gap by studying the structure of GeNTK across many models. Formulating the model state as the solution to a global implicit constraint, we derive GeNTK as a product of two operators: K, accounting for immediate parameter-to-state interactions, and P, describing internal state-to-state dependencies. For a broad class of "weight-based models", such as RNNs and transformers, we prove a universal Kronecker-core theorem showing that K admits an exact, forward-pass-computable form given by the Gram matrix of weight-site variables. This core gives a measurable state-dependent restriction on Euclidean GD, termed "self-referential bias": current activity filters which adjoint directions can drive a first-order update. For recurrent models (GRUs and RNNs), we examine the spectrum of GeNTK and formalize notions of low-rank, biased learning in terms of reduced spatial or temporal ranks of the full operator. Practically, this explains why some RNN initializations yield better learning, while some plateau, by biasing the GeNTK and thus restricting learning to a small domain of learnable tasks. To demonstrate computational viability, we validate the main theorems in a self-attention transformer and a pretrained Pythia transformer language model with 410 million parameters. Overall, our results expose tractable local rank and mode-selective biases in the finite-width GD geometry and open the door to principled study of the GeNTK, a bridge between theory and practice.

    中文

    在使用梯度下降（GD）训练神经网络时，每次迭代都会产生一个线性算子，用来控制模型内部状态变量的一阶更新。我们将此算子称为全局经验神经切线核（GeNTK）。在有限宽度网络中，GeNTK 通常难以构造，因此先前工作主要关注受限情形，例如只跟踪输出或研究无限宽度极限。在此，我们通过研究多个模型中 GeNTK 的结构弥合这一差距。我们将模型状态表述为全局隐式约束的解，并推导出 GeNTK 是两个算子的乘积：K 描述即时的参数到状态交互，P 描述内部状态之间的依赖关系。对于一大类“基于权重的模型”（如 RNN 和 Transformer），我们证明了一个普适的 Kronecker 核心定理：K 存在一种精确且可由前向传播计算的形式，即权重位置变量的 Gram 矩阵。这个核心给出了对欧氏 GD 的一种可测量的、依赖于状态的限制，我们称之为“自指偏置”：当前活动会筛选出能够驱动一阶更新的伴随方向。对于循环模型（GRU 和 RNN），我们考察了 GeNTK 的谱，并根据完整算子在空间或时间方向上的秩降低，形式化定义了低秩、有偏学习的概念。实际而言，这解释了为何某些 RNN 初始化带来更好的学习效果，而另一些会陷入平台期：它们通过使 GeNTK 产生偏置，将学习限制在一个小范围的可学习任务中。为证明计算上的可行性，我们在自注意力 Transformer 和一个拥有 4.1 亿参数的预训练 Pythia Transformer 语言模型上验证了主要定理。总体而言，我们的结果揭示了有限宽度 GD 几何中可处理的局部秩和模式选择偏置，并为系统研究 GeNTK 开辟了道路，搭起了理论与实践之间的桥梁。

    PIVOT：通过轨迹优化衔接 LLM 智能体的规划与执行

    Tuo Zhang and Alin-Ionut Popa and Yan Xu and Rui Song and Dimitrios Dimitriadis

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    PIVOT iteratively improves agent plans using execution feedback, with a monotonic acceptance rule and empirical gains in constraint satisfaction. This substantially advances planning and agent task execution; trajectory refinement has an incidental connection to composition, but the abstract does not study compositional representations or generalization.

    PIVOT 利用执行反馈反复改进智能体规划，并通过单调接受规则和实证结果提高约束满足度。这显著推动了规划和智能体任务执行的发展；轨迹优化与组合性存在附带联系，但摘要并未研究组合式表征或泛化。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Large language model (LLM)-based agents frequently generate seemingly coherent plans that fail upon execution due to infeasible actions, constraint violations, and compounding errors over extended horizons. PIVOT (Plan-Inspect-eVOlve Trajectories) addresses this plan-execution misalignment through a self-supervised framework that treats trajectories as optimizable objects iteratively refined via environment interaction. The framework comprises four stages: PLAN generates candidate trajectories; INSPECT executes them and computes structured losses with textual gradients encoding plan-execution discrepancies; EVOLVE applies these signals to produce improved trajectories; and VERIFY performs a final global check against task constraints. A monotonic acceptance process ensures a non-decreasing solution quality. Empirical evaluations on DeepPlanning and GAIA demonstrate state-of-the-art performance: with human-in-the-loop (HITL) feedback, PIVOT establishes a strong upper bound up to 94% relative improvement in constraint satisfaction, while its fully autonomous variant retains substantial gains, showing that the core trajectory-refinement mechanism remains effective without external supervision. At the same time, PIVOT remains computationally efficient, requiring up to 3x to 5x fewer tokens than competing refinement methods. These findings establish that (self- or human-supervised) feedback-based trajectory optimization is a principled methodology for mitigating plan-execution gaps in autonomous agent systems.

To address this challenge, we introduce Bot-Mod a moderation framework that grounds detection in agent intent rather than traditional content-level signals. Bot-Mod interrogates a target agent using a fixed set of diagnostic probes and infers its intent through Bayesian posterior inference over candidate intents.     The paper studies privacy and utility in releasing transformer hidden states, deriving Gaussian-release limits and a minimax diagonal mechanism, then showing architecture–release co-design can improve privacy.     本文研究 Transformer 隐藏状态发布中的隐私与效用，推导了高斯发布的限制和一种极小极大对角机制，并进一步表明架构与发布的协同设计能够改善隐私。隐藏状态这一主题与可解释性的联系只是附带的，而架构和机制方面的结果则对模型系统提供了实质性见解。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Of $1{,}536$ Gaussian release covariances we tested for single-layer hidden-state privacy, zero achieve both moderate utility and moderate privacy against an adaptive retrieval attacker. We prove a complementary Fisher-ball lower bound: every full-rank Gaussian release at $O(1)$ Fisher utility admits a direction whose Mahalanobis signal grows linearly in hidden width, ruling out uniform Gaussian safety in the class and matching the empirical empty middle. The diagonal inverse-Fisher release $\Sigma^\star_{\mathrm{diag}}(\mathcal{K}) = (2\mathcal{K}/d)\,\mathrm{diag}(1/F_{ii})$ is the unique minimax-optimal diagonal mechanism at first-order KL budget $\mathcal{K}$ and the only release with worst-attacker top-1 $\le 0.001$ at every point of a 32 model-layer grid, but it sits on a privacy/utility edge rather than filling the middle. A generalized-eigen mechanism reaching $13\times$ Pareto reduction under Euclidean retrieval collapses to $100\%$ top-1 under the adaptive Mahalanobis attacker, and a full-trajectory sequence inverter recovers $94\%$ of clean GPT-2 prefixes but $0\%$ under $\Sigma_{\mathrm{diag}}$. A split-memory transformer trained from scratch reaches $G_{\mathrm{Mah}} \in [20, 33]$ at 90M and maintains a $6$--$24\times$ advantage over same-budget GPT baselines from 30M to 1B at a fixed-token language-modeling loss penalty; pretrained models top out at 9.3. These results reframe hidden-state release from mechanism-design within the Gaussian class to architecture or release co-design.

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Neural language models are typically trained on next-token prediction, although linguistic structure spans multiple temporal scales. Successor representations (SRs) make this horizon explicit by encoding discounted distributions over future states. Here, we ask whether such predictive representations can recover not only word classes, but also finer functional and construction-like structure from natural language. A residual network trained on WikiText-103 predicts SR distributions at three horizons without part-of-speech supervision. At the shortest horizon, unsupervised clustering robustly recovers nouns, verbs, and adjectives, while directed inter-cluster transitions reproduce familiar syntactic asymmetries. At finer resolutions and across 13 part-of-speech categories, the same geometry reveals semantic-functional groupings that cross category boundaries and directed relations tracing candidate date, measurement, and title-name constructions. Part-of-speech agreement declines as the predictive horizon lengthens. These results suggest that word classes are coarse regions within a richer predictive geometry in which categorical and construction-like linguistic structure emerge from future-word distributions.

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Multi-agent reasoning systems adopt a generate-then-transfer paradigm that forces end-to-end latency to scale linearly with pipeline depth. We introduce StreamMA, a multi-agent reasoning system that streams each reasoning step to downstream agents as soon as it is generated, pipelining adjacent agents and thus reducing latency. Surprisingly, this pipelining also improves effectiveness: because multi-step reasoning quality is non-uniform and early steps are more reliable than later ones, working with these reliable early steps instead of the full chain prevents error-prone late steps from misleading downstream agents. We formalize both advantages with the first closed-form joint analysis of stream, serial, and single protocols, deriving the effectiveness ordering, speedup upper bound, and cost ratio. Across eight reasoning benchmarks spanning mathematics, science, and code, three frontier LLMs (Claude Opus 4.6, GPT-5.4, and GLM-5.2), and three topologies (Chain, Tree, Graph), StreamMA outperforms both baselines (avg.+7.3pp, max +22.4pp on HMMT2026; Claude Opus 4.6-High). Beyond these contributions, we discover a step-level scaling law: increasing per-agent steps consistently improves both effectiveness and efficiency, a new scaling dimension orthogonal to and composable with agent-count scaling.

Comparing V-JEPA and VideoMAE further shows that most gains arise from natural-video temporal context, with feature-level latent prediction providing a smaller additional benefit. These trends transfer across robotic benchmarks, though CALVIN reveals that static-environment tasks can partially mask the importance of temporal structure by allowing strong image priors to suffice.     本文评估了掩码扩散语言模型的基于置信度的重掩码，并发现它对准确率和多样性的影响取决于解码条件，而模型本身似乎才是瓶颈。这是一项实质性的推理时计算研究；它与推理能力的联系仅限于生成质量和纠正采样错误，并未涉及推理能力本身。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Masked diffusion language models (dLLMs) have recently emerged as a competitive alternative to autoregressive language models, with the promise of faster inference via parallel token generation. A notable limitation of the masked formulation, however, is that once a token has been unmasked it can no longer be revised, leaving dLLMs vulnerable to early sampling mistakes. Confidence-based remasking methods aim to address this in a training-free manner by revising low-confidence tokens, with encouraging early results. In this work, we compare the accuracy-compute Pareto frontiers of three such methods (WINO, Saber, and COVER) to those of confidence-based unmasking alone (Fast-dLLM). We find that under greedy decoding, all three perform on par with Fast-dLLM at commonly used shorter block lengths; gains of remasking appear only at longer block lengths, where confidence-based unmasking is known to degrade. Under stochastic decoding, WINO reduces generation diversity beyond that of unmasking alone, while it helps recover from errors introduced by learned Bernoulli unmasking policies. Our results show that the benefits of confidence-based remasking are highly setting-dependent, underscoring the need for more comprehensive evaluation. Finally, our analyses point to the dLLM, not the remasking rule, as the bottleneck, suggesting that effective remasking may require changes to training, not only to inference.

    中文

    掩码扩散语言模型（dLLM）近来已成为自回归语言模型的一种有竞争力的替代方案，其优势在于能够通过并行生成 token 加快推理。然而，掩码形式有一个显著局限：token 一旦解除掩码便无法再修改，使 dLLM 容易受到早期采样错误的影响。基于置信度的重掩码方法试图以无需训练的方式解决这一问题，即修改低置信度 token，早期结果令人鼓舞。在本研究中，我们将三种此类方法（WINO、Saber 和 COVER）的准确率—计算量 Pareto 前沿，与仅采用基于置信度的解除掩码方法（Fast-dLLM）进行比较。我们发现，在贪心解码下，常用的较短块长度中，这三种方法的表现都与 Fast-dLLM 相当；只有在较长块长度下，重掩码才有提升，而在这种情况下，众所周知基于置信度的解除掩码表现会下降。在随机解码下，WINO 相比仅解除掩码的方法进一步降低了生成多样性；但它有助于修正学习得到的伯努利解除掩码策略引入的错误。我们的结果表明，基于置信度的重掩码能否带来益处高度依赖具体设置，凸显了开展更全面评估的必要性。最后，我们的分析指出，瓶颈在于 dLLM 本身，而非重掩码规则；这表明有效的重掩码可能需要改变训练，而不只是改变推理。

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

Its causal head attribution is transferable mechanistic evidence, while reasoning preservation is a substantial target; the focus is not on compositional generalization, and pruning is a useful systems technique rather than a central systems-design contribution.

    ENGLISH

    Large language models (LLMs) excel at multi-step reasoning but incur substantial inference cost. We introduce Causal Attribution Pruning (CAP), a training-free method that identifies critical attention heads by measuring their causal impact on reasoning tasks and uses these head-level scores to guide fine-grained weight pruning. For each attention head, CAP estimates the expected performance degradation when the head is masked during forward passes on a small calibration set of reasoning problems. These causal scores are then converted into weight-level importance values for the corresponding projection matrices. Unlike magnitude-only or activation-based criteria, CAP's interventional measurement directly captures each head's functional contribution, yielding relative accuracy gains of up to 61% over Wanda on ARC-Challenge at 20% sparsity. We evaluate CAP on GSM8K, StrategyQA, and ARC-Challenge using Llama-3-8B-Instruct and Mistral-7B-Instruct at 10%, 20%, and 50% sparsity. At moderate sparsity (10-20%), CAP improves over Wanda in most model-benchmark configurations. with especially large gains on ARC-Challenge for Llama-3. Our results suggest that attention-head-level causal attribution can better preserve reasoning performance on downstream benchmarks than correlational pruning criteria at equivalent sparsity, while remaining limited by coarse MLP attribution at 50% sparsity.

    Existing LLM logical-reasoning benchmarks largely focus on object-level inference under fixed predicates and rules, leaving higher-order reasoning over rules and policies underexplored. Beyond answer accuracy, HOLogicBench provides solver-verified reference reasoning paths for each instance, enabling fine-grained evaluation of model-generated reasoning against valid derivations.     Big goals are hard to achieve all at once; breaking them into small steps is wiser. We present Trust Region Policy Distillation (TOP-D), which transforms the notoriously unstable, high-variance On-Policy Distillation (OPD) into a stable training paradigm by dynamically constructing a proximal teacher. Theoretically, we establish a rigorous framework demonstrating that TOP-D inherently controls gradient variance. By providing a formal global convergence analysis alongside a monotonic improvement bound, we mathematically formalize the reliability and stability of the overall training dynamics. Empirically, TOP-D dramatically enhances training stability, sample efficiency, and final performance on mathematical reasoning tasks. More importantly, TOP-D introduces zero additional computational overhead, positioning itself as a promising alternative to the well-established OPD paradigm.
